title: Heading for the Stallbook product page
question: Which heading and sub-line should open the product page?

recommended.reason: it is the only one that tells a stallholder what they get, in their own terms, before it says how.

options.name: Says what it is
options.note: A plain label for the product; the shortest heading, and the least to react to.

sample.heading: Bookkeeping for market stalls
sample.sub: Record each sale as you make it, and see what every market day earned after stall fees and stock.

options.name: Leads with the result
options.note: Opens on the moment the product pays off: knowing the day's profit at closing time.

sample.heading: Know what Saturday earned before you pack up
sample.sub: Stallbook adds up sales, stall fees and stock as you go, so the day's profit is on your phone at closing time.

options.name: Names the pain
options.note: Starts from the mess it replaces; warmer and more casual, and vaguer about what the product does.

sample.heading: No more shoebox of receipts
sample.sub: Photograph a receipt, tap a sale, and Stallbook keeps the books a market stall needs.

options.name: One concrete claim
options.note: Commits to a single measurable promise about speed and signal; the longest heading.

sample.heading: Record a sale in two taps, with or without signal
sample.sub: Built for a busy stall: large buttons, works offline, and a total for each market day.

context.footnote: No card needed. Works offline at the stall.
